name: Mam tom cha
summary: Mắm tôm chà is a Gò Công specialty, not a Mỹ Tho stall. The Tiền Giang provincial portal eats it with bún, boiled pork, unripe banana, sour starfruit, cucumber, and herbs. Thanh Niên, 27 Aug 2014, prints a family method and a nearly 200-year line the portal does not print.
origin: Gò Công. The Tiền Giang provincial portal calls it the specialty of that town.
history: Thanh Niên, 27 Aug 2014, says that nearly 200 years earlier the paste followed Empress Từ Dụ to the Huế court and was served to the Nguyễn kings in the first half of the 19th century. The Tiền Giang provincial portal does not print that line.
culture: The provincial portal calls mắm tôm chà the specialty of Gò Công. It is not a Mỹ Tho bowl.
Thanh Niên says Gò Công then had about a dozen commercial workshops, each with a family method.
texture: Thanh Niên says a good jar keeps for a year. The provincial portal does not describe the texture.
taste: Thanh Niên says the mixed dip should be sour, sweet, hot, and salty in balance, and that vinegar takes the edge off the smell. The herbs it names are mint, bean sprouts, garlic chives, perilla, lettuce, cucumber, and especially unripe banana and green starfruit.
howToEat: The provincial portal says to eat it with bún, boiled pork, unripe banana, sour starfruit, cucumber, and whatever herbs are on the table.

Thanh Niên says a basic method, and that each house differs: clean live tôm đất without losing the roe, soak in rượu nếp for about 20 minutes, drain, pound with garlic, chili, and salt, ferment for about a week, sieve out the shells, and dry the meat for about 20 sunny days. The three ingredients Thanh Niên names are live sea shrimp, pungent garlic, and ripe red chili.

Thanh Niên says the plain mắm, called y, was eaten with white rice, used as a dip for sour fish soup with tamarind leaves, or eaten with green mango and hog plum. Mixed with a little vinegar, lime, sugar, garlic, and chopped chili, it is the dip for boiled pork belly rolled with rice paper, herbs, and bún.
A price was not printed. The price is Check on arrival.
where: Gò Công. The provincial portal does not name a street in Mỹ Tho. A Mỹ Tho address is Check on arrival. One workshop address in Thanh Niên is not a pick.
seoTitle: Mam tom cha from Go Cong
seoDescription: Gò Công shrimp paste, eaten with bún and boiled pork on the Tiền Giang provincial portal. Thanh Niên prints a second method. The price is Check on arrival.
